learning_outcomes.text: Ability to solve problems within their area of study.
Ability to abstract: capacity to create and use models that reflect real situations.
Ability to plan and organize personal work.
Ability to integrate quickly and work efficiently in unidisciplinary teams and collaborate in a multidisciplinary environment.
Ability for effective oral and written communication (expression and comprehension), with special emphasis on technical documentation.
Possess the necessary learning skills to undertake further studies or improve their training with a certain degree of autonomy.
Have motivation for quality and continuous improvement and act rigorously in professional development.

syllabus_topics: Functioning of economic activity and types of markets.
Concept and objectives of the company.
Types of companies: economic, organizational and legal criteria.
Asset and results analysis for decision making.
Valuation of investment and financing projects.
teaching_methods: Case analysis from document reading and video viewing
Exposition of individual or group works
assessment_rules: In the ordinary call, the final grade is calculated as: FINAL GRADE = EX.ORD + P1 + P2 + P3 + P. A minimum of 40% (2.6 points) is required in the final exam (EX.ORD), and a minimum of 1.4 points in the sum of P1, P2, P3, and P. If all minimums are met and the total grade is at least 5 points, the course is passed. If a minimum is not met but the total is over 5, the final grade is 4.5 points; if the practicals minimum is not met, the final grade is 'Fail' if the student sits the final exam. For extraordinary calls, students can take a theoretical-practical exam (EX.EXTR, max 6.5 points, min 40%) and/or a practical exam (EX.PR, max 3.5 points, min 40%). Grades from the ordinary call (EX.ORD, P1, P2, P3, P) can be carried over if their respective minimums were met.
